purpose: Paired synthetic commit/run histories frozen for the process-signals signal study. Each scenario is one neutral history fed to both builder arms (python/cogbench/src/cogbench/process.py and apps/portal/worker/services/process-signals.ts). Histories are frozen: the study never invents data at run time, so a replay regenerates from exactly these bytes.

encoding.commits: Neutral form. authoredAt is an ISO-8601 UTC string with optional fractional seconds. The Python arm passes it through unchanged (process.py consumes ISO-8601); the TypeScript arm converts to epoch milliseconds with Date.parse (process-signals.ts consumes numbers). filesChanged, sha and authorLogin pass through unchanged. coAuthors is the raw Co-authored-by trailer list; only the TypeScript arm resolves it against the roster (documented divergence). insertions/deletions are carried so the study can demonstrate neither arm reads them.
encoding.runs: Neutral form. createdAt is the instant the run finished scoring; the Python arm maps it to Run.created_at and the TypeScript arm to RunRecord.finishedAt (the TS module's documented mapping: first light is when a run finished and scored). runId and status are carried so the study can demonstrate neither arm reads them.
encoding.week: Week label selecting the default stage map, or null. Null mirrors the TypeScript orchestrator's rule that a team with no runs yet has no knowable stage map; the Python arm implements the same rule with an empty caller-supplied stage map.
encoding.fetchFailure: Present only when the scenario exercises the TypeScript-only fetch-failed arm ({"ok": false, "reason": ...}). The Python module has no input that can produce this state, so that scenario has no Python arm.
encoding.truncated: True when the commit window is known to be truncated. The Python module has no truncation input, so the Python arm never reports a window; this is a disclosed arm-only field.

scenarios.notes: Ordinary spread-out development: three authors, five stages touched except fanout, first light on 2026-10-04, one boundary commit after it. Window truncated in the TS arm so the untouched-fanout absence is ambiguous by construction.
Whole project pushed as one commit (the real failure two of five capstone teams hit). Per-commit attribution is meaningless; every commit-derived signal must refuse, while run history still counts.
Repository connected but no recorded commits; one scored run exists.
Bulk upload by share, not by count: three commits, but the first holds 10 of 12 changed files (83% > 60% threshold).
Real, usable commit history but the team has never run anything, so no week label is knowable. Both arms must degrade stage footprint and ownership to empty without treating it as a data failure.

Co-authored-by trailers. One trailer resolves to roster member eli via the roster email; one trailer names a bot and must be dropped. Known, documented divergence: the TypeScript arm resolves trailers against the roster, the Python module does not (single author_login per commit).
Boundary churn is strictly-after first light: one contract commit exactly at the first-light instant is excluded, one 1 millisecond later is included, one before is excluded.

TypeScript-only arm: the commit fetch failed with an authorization error. The Python module has no input that can produce this state, so this scenario has no Python arm; it exists so the TS arm's honest-unavailable path is measured rather than assumed.
The largest commit holds exactly 60% of changed files (6 of 10). The bulk-upload threshold is strictly greater-than, so this history must classify as usable, not bulk_upload.

Runs exist but none has ever scored, so first light is null and there is no first-light anchor for churn. Harness assumption, recorded here: an all-unscored run list is treated as week-unknown, mirroring the no-runs degradation, because a week label is resolved from run evidence in this study.

ablations.singleVariable: one commit's file paths stop matching the query stage
ablations.expected: query stage commit_count drops 1 -> 0 in both arms; no other stage moves

ablations.singleVariable: the first run loses its scored flag
ablations.expected: firstScoredAt moves to the second run in both arms; scoredRunCount 3 -> 2; churn unchanged (the surviving boundary commit is still after the new first light)

ablations.singleVariable: one commit gains a Co-authored-by trailer that resolves to roster member blake
ablations.expected: TypeScript arm: spectrogram and peaks distinct-author counts include blake, ownership lists gain blake. Python arm: no change (single author_login per commit). This is the documented ported divergence, not a defect.

no signal change in either arm: both modules accept these fields and no function in either reads them. A zero-delta measurement is the expected outcome, and it cannot rule out reading in code paths this history never reaches.

ablations.singleVariable: the first run's status string changes to 'failed'
ablations.expected: no signal change in either arm: status is accepted input that no signal reads. Same inconclusive-by-design caveat as ablate-insertions.

ablations.singleVariable: the post-first-light boundary commit moves to before first light
ablations.expected: boundary churn 1 event -> 0 events in both arms; stage footprints unchanged (the commit matched no stage)
all three deltas land at once; the combined result cannot attribute any observed change to a single cause. Included precisely to show why single-variable ablation is the study's unit of evidence.
